To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) astroglial cells are involved in AD pathogenesis, but they also play a neuroprotective and/or neurorepair role; (2) microglial cells participate in AD pathogenesis but they also contribute to neuroprotection; (3) the neuroprotective role is exerted in a time-dependent fashion, and (4) the neuroprotecting role can be enhanced by pharmacological interventions
the astroglial response is the most important factor in determining the fate of the neurons in AD.
The neuroglial responses to AD are not homogeneous, they are region and type-dependent, but also concurrent, with both neuroprotective and neurodegenerative effects".
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of neuroglial cells, their modifications and their possible implications in AD pathogenesis, diagnosis, treatment, prevention and cure.
the study of neuroglial cell alterations in AD and the possible role they play in the pathogenesis of this disease.
the study of the different types of neuroglial cells, their modifications and their responses in the context of AD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, although the neurodegenerative processes in AD involve the whole brain, there are different and specific neuroglial alterations that are regionally and locally dependent.
neuroglia is not only a passive bystander in the AD process, but that it actively participates in the pathogenesis of the disease, and that it can be considered a therapeutic target.
, in AD, the brain is not a homogeneous organ, but a mosaic of local and regional neuro-protective and neurodegenerative processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
neuroglial cells are not only involved in the pathogenesis of AD, they are also essential to the development of new therapeutic strategies.

neuroglial cells, as well as neurons, have the ability to change their morphology and function in response to the different environmental stimuli, but the exact meaning of the changes is not well understood yet.
the glial cell alterations in AD are not a simple consequence of neuronal damage, but they are also a primary cause of neuronal death and/or a consequence of the neurodegenerative process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the different neuroglia types, with their different functions, are involved in the different stages and aspects of AD.
neuroglial cells are not only the passive bystanders in AD, but are actively involved in the pathogenesis of AD and, therefore, in the development of new therapeutic approaches.
the neuroglial response to AD, and the possible role it fulfills, depends on the type of neuroglial cell and the specific brain region in which it is found.
